name: MonarchSiteShell
title: SiteHeader and SiteFooter
wrapsNative: NavigationStack with a ScrollView and .navigationTitle for the brand; ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .primaryAction) for the actions and a Menu of the links (a nested Menu per group); MonarchSiteFooter is a LazyVGrid of link columns
summary: The frame of a product's public or about screens in an app: a navigation bar with the brand, the site's links in a standard menu and the account actions, then the scrolling content and a footer of link columns and the legal line.
whenToUse: For the signed-out or about screens of an app that mirror the product's website: product links, pricing, log in and get started.
whenNotToUse: For the signed-in app, use a TabView or NavigationSplitView. For Rook's own company bar, use MonarchRookBar. For one link list, use a List.
api: init(_ brand: String, navigation: [MonarchSiteNavItem] = [], footer: MonarchSiteFooter? = nil, menuLabel: String? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)
init(_ brand: String, navigation: [MonarchSiteNavItem] = [], footer: MonarchSiteFooter? = nil, menuLabel: String? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)  // where Actions == EmptyView

options.name: brand
options.description: The product or company name, shown as the navigation title (a large title on iPhone).

options.name: navigation
options.description: Links and groups of links, shown in the bar's menu; a group is a submenu whose items show their descriptions.

options.name: menuLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Menu" of the menu button.

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons at the trailing edge of the bar, such as Log in and Get started.

options.name: content
options.description: The screen's content, in a vertical scroll view.

states.name: bar
states.description: The brand as the navigation title; actions and the menu button at the trailing edge of the bar.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A standard menu of the links; a group opens as a submenu.

states.name: footer
states.description: Link columns side by side when they fit, then a divider and the legal line.

appearance: The bar and the title are the system navigation bar's. Footer column titles use the default text colour; footer links and the legal line the muted text colour. Colours come from theme roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web SiteHeader is a sticky page header with a row of links and dropdowns, a mobile menu dialog and a skip target; SiteFooter is the page footer. On iOS the header is the system navigation bar of a NavigationStack: the links are a standard Menu (a row of links does not fit a phone), the actions are bar buttons and pushed screens get the system back button. Android does not ship this component.
accessibility: The brand is the navigation title, read as the screen's heading.
The menu button is named "Menu" (or menuLabel); groups are submenus and each link is a menu item read with its description.
The bar's actions stay separate buttons.
Footer column titles have the header trait; each footer link is a link at least 44 points tall.
edgeCases: A long brand wraps or is shortened by the navigation bar, as any navigation title.
More than two actions crowd the bar on a phone; keep one primary action and put the rest in the menu.
Footer columns wrap to one per row at large text sizes.
